# SCSE3040 --- Lab Practicals

**Machine Learning Operations · B.Tech CSE 5th Semester · Bennett University
· Session 2026-27**

Fourteen practicals, one per fortnight, all building the same running project:
a **food delivery-time predictor**. Each one picks up exactly where the last
one stopped, so the arc across the semester is

> notebook -> package -> tracked experiments -> API -> container -> cluster
> -> logs -> automated pipeline -> monitoring -> retrain on drift

*This file is generated by `scripts/build_labs.py`. Edit the practicals in
`scripts/labdefs/`, not here.*

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | Any laptop with **8 GB of RAM**. Nothing here needs a GPU. |
| Disk | About 3 GB free, most of it for Docker in P08. |
| Software | The course virtual environment --- see [SETUP.md](SETUP.md). |
| Internet | Only for the one-time setup, and for P08's first image build. |

Only **P08** needs anything beyond the course environment: Docker Desktop.
P09 runs real `kubectl` commands if a cluster happens to be available, but
every graded task in it works without one.

Several practicals draw charts with matplotlib, and a few add **sliders** if
the optional `ipywidgets` library is installed (SETUP.md installs it). Without
it those cells still run and draw the static version; nothing breaks.

## How a practical works

Every notebook has the same three parts, in this order.

1. **Walkthrough.** Numbered steps you read and run. It works as shipped, so
   your teacher can project it and demonstrate. Nothing here can be got wrong.
2. **Your turn.** Three tasks. Each has a stub with `# TODO` in it and a hint.
   Do them in order; they get harder.
3. **Self-check.** One cell that marks your work and prints a `PASS`/`FAIL`
   table. Run it as often as you like --- it never breaks your notebook, and a
   task you have not started simply shows `FAIL`.

## Running a practical

```
cd labs\P01-workbench
..\..\.venv\Scripts\python -m jupyter lab P01.ipynb
```

Then work down the notebook, pressing **Shift + Enter** in each cell. Always
run the cells in order from the top.

If everything goes wrong: **Kernel -> Restart Kernel and Clear All Outputs**,
then start again from the first cell. Nothing is damaged by doing this.

## For faculty

Each folder holds three files:

| File | For | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| `PNN.ipynb` | students | the practical itself |
| `README.md` | students | the handout: aim, background, marking |
| `FACULTY.md` | **you only** | timing plan, expected output, common mistakes, troubleshooting, and the answers |

**`FACULTY.md` contains the answers. Do not circulate it.**

You do not need prior MLOps experience to run these. Each `FACULTY.md` gives a
minute-by-minute plan, the exact output a correct run produces, what students
get wrong and what to say when they do. Read the handout once and run the
notebook yourself before the session --- it runs top to bottom without edits.

Grading is done from the self-check table the last cell prints. You do not
need to read student code line by line.

## Checking the practicals still work

```
.venv\Scripts\python scripts\build_labs.py            # regenerate all 14
.venv\Scripts\python scripts\check_lab.py --all       # QA all 14
```

`check_lab.py` runs each notebook **twice**: once exactly as students receive
it, and once with the reference answers pasted in, where it must score full
marks. It also checks peak memory against the 8 GB budget and fails any cell
that takes too long for a lab period.

Run it after upgrading any library. It is the fastest way to find out that a
new scikit-learn has changed an answer.
